Entity.Title: School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa

Title: PhD research dissemination workshop
NewsSummary: Ms Eunice S. Pallangyo, a Tanzania based midwifery tutor presents her research findings on Improved Postpartum Care after a Participatory Facilitation Intervention in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.

content.text: Ms Eunice S. Pallangyo, a Tanzania based midwifery tutor nearing the end of her PhD programme, recently disseminated her research entitled, Improved Postpartum Care after a Participatory Facilitation Intervention in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania: A Mixed Method Evaluation, to an audience of stakeholders on July 11, 2017. Joe Lugalla, Director of the Institute for Educational Development East Africa (IEDEA) at AKU, delivered welcoming remarks. He emphasised the importance of disseminating research as a way to share ideas to improve the health of mothers and newborns. Dr Columba, Academic Head at SONAM-Tanzania, spoke about previous studies that highlighted the limited postpartum care (PPC) services in the country and recommendations to strengthen these services. In Tanzania, PPC is an uncommon service that is regarded as an afterthought, leading to poor outcomes for mothers and newborns.

The Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey (2016) reported 556 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births and 25 newborn deaths per 1,000 live births; numbers that are exceedingly high. To better understand barriers to PPC, Ms Pallangyo conducted research in Ilala and Temeke, two low-income suburbs located in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. She aimed to: 1) assess knowledge, attitudes and practices of healthcare providers; and 2) explore healthcare providers' perceptions of current PPC practice and its potential for improvement. In total, 60 government-owned health institutions (31 in Ilala and 29 in Temeke) were surveyed. The results showed that healthcare providers had high knowledge and positive attitudes toward PPC. However, the majority of health institutions reported no PPC consultations, and only seven institutions reported monthly PPC consultations. The study highlights that awareness and resources are needed to support implementation of PPC services. Ms Pallangyo stated, 'While top-down approach to leadership is dominant in the health system, there is a need to combine this, to a small extent at least, with a bottom- up approach. This way, healthcare providers' views will be incorporated in healthcare, and probably they may become more responsive. They know better the context...what works and what doesn't work'.  Attending stakeholders, including government officials, were appreciative of the research findings and stressed the need for more research to influence budget and policy-making decisions.

SONAM would like to convey a special thank you to stakeholders from surrounding communities and institutions that attended and participated in the workshop. Notably, Mr Gustav P. Moyo, Director of Nursing and Midwifery Services at the Ministry of Health; Mr Ndementria Vermand, Assistant Director of Nursing Training at the Ministry of Health; Professor Joe Lugalla, Director at IEDEA, AKU; Professor William Macharia, Associate Dean, Research, AKU-Faculty of Health Sciences; Mr Amiri R Mmaka, Dean, School of Nursing at Hubert Kairuki Memorial University; Ms Agnes Massae, representing the Dean, School of Nursing at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences; representative district medical officers of Ilala and Temeke; representative regional nursing officers; representative regional reproductive and child health coordinators; representative district nursing officers from Ilala and Temeke; representatives from Jhpiego; and all heads of health facilities in Ilala district. The School would also like to thank the National Institute of Medical Research Review Committee in Tanzania for ethics approval, and the Municipal Councils and heads of institutions for permission to conduct the research studies in the two suburbs. Furthermore, this project would not have been possible without collaborative funding from SONAM in Tanzania and Uppsala University in Sweden.
